[USER] User inquired about the effect of camera angles in horror films on audience suspense levels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Camera angles in horror films are influential in building suspense and can significantly impact the audience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Low-angle shots produce feelings of vulnerability for the audience, making characters seem larger or more intimidating.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] High-angle shots can make a character look smaller and more vulnerable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Close-up shots in horror films typically show a character's face or a particular object in detail, making the scene feel more intense and intimidating.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tracking or panning shots can create an unsettling feeling in the audience, increasing suspense as the audience doesn't know what will happen next.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The right camera angles in horror films play a significant role in creating suspense and tension, manipulating the audience's emotions.  
[USER] User asked if camera angles alone can make a horror movie scary or if they are just one part of the puzzle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Camera angles are just one element of creating suspense and fear in horror films.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A horror movie requires multiple elements to be truly scary, including storytelling, music and sound effects, lighting, character development, and special effects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Camera angles alone cannot make a horror movie scary if other elements are not included in the film's production.  
[USER] User requested an example of a horror film where camera angles played a significant role in building suspense.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example is the 1960 horror-thriller "Psycho," directed by Alfred Hitchcock.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In "Psycho," Hitchcock uses quick, close-up shots of the killer's knife in the famous shower scene to build tension.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An overhead shot shows the bloody water swirling around the drain, adding to the sense of disorientation and chaos.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A low-angle shot when the killer approaches the victim creates a sense of vulnerability for the audience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A high-angle shot shows the victim's lifeless body on the shower floor, adding to the feeling of horror and shock.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The camera angles in "Psycho" effectively created suspense and terror that are still considered remarkable today.
